content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide should be administered orally in doses of 10-20 mL between meals and at bedtime for individuals over 12 years of age. The safety and efficacy of these agents have not been established for children under 12 years of age. 2. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated. Avoid using pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but antacid and pazopanib dosing should be separated by several hours. 3. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of raltegravir through cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Co-administration is contraindicated and not recommended, even with dose separation. 4. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to reduced plasma concentrations. Administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after antacids or buffered medications. 5. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil through cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, reducing absorption. Studies in monkeys showed significant decreases in plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 6. Magnesium hydroxide also decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil through cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, reducing absorption. Studies in monkeys showed significant decreases in plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. 7. Aluminum hydroxide reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours. 8.
